definitions.meaning: a plight is a difficult fix or predicament
a naughty, impish youngster is called this affectionately

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about the troubles caused by a naughty youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a tricky predicament, and an affectionate word for an impish youngster.

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned around and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend shares thoughts on the sport of swordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A palisade is a fence of stakes, so fencing in the sense of a barrier.

indicators.note: to confuse is to mix up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A clever person can bewilder a moth.
explanation.definitionFit: The cinnabar is a red-and-black day-flying moth, named after the red mineral.

indicators.note: in a down clue up means each piece is read bottom to top

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a notice
nil means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone sees nothing doing with a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole run AD NIL backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Linda is a woman's first name, standing for any girl.

clue.text: Deny agent arranged to get Lincoln out

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order, as things arranged are

parts.note: taken as written
Abe is the familiar short name of President Abraham Lincoln

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to let an operative organise Lincoln's escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles AGENT together with ABE, the nickname of Abraham Lincoln; 'to get' and 'out' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: To abnegate is to renounce or refuse oneself something, a formal synonym of deny.

parts.note: a life of minimal means, punning on unclothed living among naturists

explanation.definitionFit: A bare existence is a life with only the barest essentials, punningly an undressed one.

clue.text: Urge to hand over morning to sandwich filling

parts.note: to egg on is to urge

indicators.note: the word hand is turned over, its first letter carried round to the back

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Encouraging someone to give a breakfast for a sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the word for hand over, carrying its first letter round to the back; 'Urge' is the verb meaning to egg on.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg and ham is a common combination put between slices of bread.

definitions.meaning: an offensive is a military assault

explanation.definitionFit: An attack is both an offensive in war and a strongly hostile piece of criticism.

parts.note: the close of something is its end
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Putting up with living near a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure something is to bear it, the same as to tolerate it.

indicators.note: the point is attached to the end of the occupation, joined on after it

parts.note: a line is a line of work, a trade or occupation
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Advice to point out the substance of a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is a woven fabric made from flax, so a type of cloth or material.

clue.text: Rate dodge made to seem disreputable

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, a reworking signal here

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who avoided paying their rates has been shamed.
explanation.walkthrough: RATE DODGE is reworked; 'made' signals that and the rest defines the past participle.
explanation.definitionFit: To derogate is to disparage or detract from someone's standing, making them appear discreditable.

definitions.meaning: resolve as a noun means firmness of purpose
backbone figuratively means strength of character

explanation.surface: A decision to display courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Determination is firmness of purpose, synonymous with both resolve and backbone.

clue.text: Conflict involving sailor in American port

indicators.note: the sailor is placed in the port, one piece going inside the other

parts.note: Seattle is a port city in Washington State
AB, able seaman, is a standard abbreviation for a sailor

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out involving a seaman ashore in a US harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval engagement is a military conflict fought at sea between fleets.

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
R, from Latin rex, abbreviates king

explanation.surface: A monarch finds a holiday town more agreeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicer is the comparative of nice, meaning more agreeable or pleasant.

clue.text: Honest, but uninteresting, artist wearing strange tights

parts.note: a dead party or town is dull, lacking interest

indicators.note: the tights go round the artist like clothing worn, so one piece encloses the other
strange signals the letters are in an odd, altered order

parts.note: taken as written
RA, Royal Academician, stands for an artist

explanation.surface: A dull painter in peculiar hosiery is called straightforward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' scrambles the hosiery word, and 'wearing' has the artist dressed in it; 'but' only links the two definitions-looking halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead straight means completely frank and upright, an informal word for honest.

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A journalists' outing is organised for entertainers.
explanation.definitionFit: Strippers are entertainers who undress on stage, a kind of performer.

parts.note: a ducat is an old gold coin
ED, editor, is a journalist

explanation.surface: A British newspaperman paid for lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Educated means schooled or instructed, the past participle matching taught.

clue.text: This dictionary is a grossly muddled publication

indicators.note: muddled means jumbled, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that a reference work is a terribly confused publication.
explanation.walkthrough: A GROSSLY is jumbled by 'muddled'; 'publication' rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossary is a list of words with their meanings, a small dictionary.

clue.text: Dire straits of doctor led astray by professional show-off

indicators.note: led astray means sent off course, so the letters wander out of order
dire means terrible, telling the next word is in a bad, jumbled state

parts.note: taken as written
MO, medical officer, is a doctor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A medic in serious trouble was misled by an exhibitionist.
explanation.walkthrough: STRAITS, MO (a doctor) and LED are mixed together, signalled by 'Dire' and 'astray'.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's model is paid to pose and display their body, a playful description of a professional exhibitionist.

clue.text: Agree to provide cloth on account

indicators.note: the cloth is put on after the account, joined on

parts.note: cord is ribbed fabric, corduroy

explanation.surface: Consenting to supply fabric on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: To accord is to be in harmony or agreement, a synonym of agree.

definitions.meaning: Sir Simon ... is a famous British conductor

explanation.definitionFit: Rattle names the British conductor Simon Rattle and a toy that amuses babies.

clue.text: Right for inclusion in theatrical hamper

indicators.note: R is to be included in the other word, placed inside it

parts.note: camp means exaggerated and theatrical in manner

explanation.surface: A stage costume basket gets a right-hand item packed into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hamper' looks like a theatre wicker basket noun but is the verb, to restrict.
explanation.definitionFit: To cramp is to restrict or confine movement, the same as to hamper.

clue.text: Declares that girl's put on weight

indicators.note: the weight is put on after the girl, added to her

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name; the 's is read as has
ounces are units of weight

explanation.surface: Someone reveals that a young woman has gained weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce is to make something known publicly, the same as to declare it.

indicators.note: the letters go about the new one, surrounding it
cryptic means puzzling, so the letters are puzzlingly mixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzling hint concerns a fresh family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic' turns CLUE into UCLE and 'about' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncle is a parent's brother, a family relative.

clue.text: Do these in sequence in addition to normal job

indicators.note: the letters are put in a fresh sequence, a rearranging signal

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to tackle tasks one after another, for a second job.
explanation.definitionFit: Work done on the side is extra employment besides one's main occupation.

clue.text: Pin said to be for surplice

indicators.note: said signals the word is spoken and the sound used

parts.note: a cotter is a pin or wedge fastening parts of a machine

explanation.surface: A fastener is supposedly meant for a church vestment.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotta is a short surplice worn by clergy and choristers, a type of white vestment.

definitions.meaning: ... a dish or a bird is getting it ready
a salad ... is a sauce poured over food

explanation.definitionFit: Dressing is the participle of dress, to prepare food, and also names a salad sauce.

clue.text: Fatal attribute of French lady, perhaps

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters may be some other arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A deadly quality belonging to a Frenchwoman, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals the letters of lady are reshuffled; 'attribute' only links, as an adjective is an attribute.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fatal causes death, which is exactly what deadly means.
